The cold deck's fit, part two

The empty composer keyed every responsive decision to the pane's WIDTH — including the ones about height — and set its one sentence as a wrapping flex row rather than as text. Below, each pane size before and after.

POD-1184 · captured from the real component and the real stylesheet at 2× · Chromium · Geist confirmed loaded

Each frame is the workspace pane alone. The shell's 48px topbar and 28px status strip are outside the crop, so a frame labelled 1200×260 shows the pane a 1200×260 window would leave — the pane heights quoted below are pane measurements, taken with that chrome in place.

What changed

  • Nothing is out of reach on a short pane. The deck centred with justify-content: center inside its own scroll container, which pushes overflow out of BOTH ends — and the start-edge half cannot be scrolled back to. At 1200×260 the sentence sat 59px above the scroller with the project picker in it. Centring is now margin-block: auto, which resolves to zero the moment free space runs out.
  • The deck compresses before it scrolls. The gap and the well were fixed pixels and the block padding was 5cqi — a width answering a height question. All three now read the window's height, which is the pane's height: the whole instrument stays on screen down to a 240px pane, and below that it scrolls from the top with every control reachable.
  • The headline is a sentence, not a flex row. A flex line break is not a text line break: the old row orphaned "in" on its own line and left the question mark floating behind a 0.4em gap. Inline flow puts the pill in the sentence as one unbreakable word, with the mark hard against it (joined by U+2060 so no line can come between them).
  • The type ramp is gentler. 4.4cqi is a pure ratio, so a 674px pane still asked for 30px of headline over three lines. It now runs from 20px to the same 33px through an offset, so the small end settles instead of shouting.

1200 × 260 — a short window

Before: the sentence sits 59px above the scroller and cannot be scrolled back to; the launch row is cut off at the other end. After: the whole instrument fits.

900 × 200 — shorter than the deck can compress to

Before: both ends clipped, nothing scrollable. After: it scrolls, and every control is reachable from one end or the other.

700 × 710 — the reported pane

Before: a 30px headline over three lines, "in" orphaned, the mark floating clear of the pill. After: one line, one sentence.

520 × 820 — a squeezed column

390 × 740 — phone width

760 × 380 — short and narrow at once

1440 × 900 — unchanged at full size

The wide deck is deliberately the same: 33px headline, 1060px measure, 132px well.

Other states, after

First-run wording, the paper theme, and a 450px pane on a 1600px window — the measures read the pane, never the window.
